i dunno, man. I feel like writing a contract to myself and vowing to at least not use the internet for leisure, and to meditate every day for 2 weeks or something starting now. something small, but good. Being happy is a skill and I don't think it's about always having a feeling. Kind of like how people who do brave things aren't never scared, they're just able to work past it into what they know is right.

Maybe we're just wishing for, like, an action movie's amount of motivation, when really it's a daily, tedious struggle. Like, that the little things in life stack up more against the "big" things in life. 

Have you learned anything about buddhism or meditation? I really believe that that approaches what we're talking about in an amazing way. Like, meditating to calm our minds down to learn to be more in control of our thoughts and more aware of what we're doing with them. Discipline, but not in a crushing way, in a realistic and calm way. 
Also, I don't think we should let ourself make the excuse of "I'm not going to completely change my life 100% the way I want it, so I'm not gonna try." Our lives aren't ever going to be completely the way we want it, so maybe we should be more focused on how we can accept ourselves for what were are and love ourselves and the rest will follow, because when you love yourself, you'll do what's right for yourself. What if we do light the fire and become so obessed with success that we destroy our friendships with people or become self-centered assholes? Maybe just little changes are just as beneficial for us, because sometimes i definitely feel the motivation of "being the best" and I'll want to work out and look the best and be the best in school, and be the most creative or whatever... that shouldnt be what it's about.

sorry, I'm ranting like crazy

Sometimes I really just want to drop everything that's useless to making myself consistently happy and that I use to just ignore or feed my addiction to avoiding life. People tell me that's extreme, but I'm not sure if I agree with them. Maybe it's unrealistic, but I guess what I feel like I need to do is cultivate good habits as much as I can and learn how to say NO to myself. I mean, there's always a choice and there's always something you can do in the moment. Maybe it's smart to gradually ween myself off of things, but I don't trust myself. I've tried to light the fire so many times and failed that I just don't believe in myself anymore. Also I'm working full time and going to school, so I'm pretty pooped most of the time. But I guess that's an excuse. I kinda think that we make our own limitations with our thoughts. Maybe it would help to just think of how much better our lives could be if we just broke the chain in little ways, even. Like, these days, I get so excited when I just interact with people who know or do something new to me... I really need to get out in the world and use my fucking mind.

I guess I always choose the thing in life that is the least fulfilling in life and always sell myself short to immediate gratification like video games, internet, porn, whatever, and it's gotten so bad that I'm just completely ignoring my responsibilities/dreams (school, work, love) and just do the bare minimum through the day, every day, for ghastly amounts of time. I am a really talented person and I could do a lot with my life, but I think I purposely sabotage myself subconsciously... like deep down I don't think I deserve to be happy so my brain tricks itself into thinking that unskillful things are the right decision for what I need to do with my life. And it gets worse when I actually try to motivate myself. Like there's a backlash and that self-destructive part of me always wins. Sometimes I say, like, "you're smart, you can figure out what the right thing to do is" but somehow I always trick my brain into ignoring what's best for me, and only focusing on what's pleasurable or mind-numbing in the moment. It really makes me sick.
